title: The Norwegian Method: A Complete Guide to Threshold Training

meta_information.core_philosophy: You do not improve by training as hard as possible. You improve by training hard enough, often enough, for long enough. Precision creates continuity, and continuity creates high-quality volume.

lactate_threshold_control.definition: Systematic monitoring and restriction of blood lactate levels during quality workouts to remain strictly at or below anaerobic threshold (OBLA).
lactate_threshold_control.mechanism: By capping lactate accumulation, athletes prevent heavy central nervous system fatigue, excessive acidosis, and prolonged muscular damage. This allows for rapid recovery and high training frequency.

target_lactate_ceilings.absolute_upper_limit: Never exceed 4.0 mmol/L during routine sub-threshold work.

morning_session_specs.rep_length_philosophy: Longer distance reps (e.g., 3k, 2k, 1 mile reps) @ controlled lower threshold pace.
morning_session_specs.physiological_purpose: Build massive aerobic volume and capillary density without neuromuscular fatigue or excessive lactate accumulation.

evening_session_specs.rep_length_philosophy: Shorter distance reps (e.g., 1000m, 800m, 400m, 200m reps) @ main threshold pace.
evening_session_specs.physiological_purpose: Sharpen threshold velocity, biomechanical turnover, and lactate clearing capacity while maintaining low central fatigue.

golden_zone_concept.definition: A conservative approach to threshold training where the athlete runs slightly slower than their absolute maximum lactate threshold to preserve recovery and consistency.

pacing_adjustments_by_track_distance.very_short_intervals_200m_400m: Executed at around actual lactate threshold pace.
pacing_adjustments_by_track_distance.short_intervals_800m_1000m: Executed approximately 1% to 3% slower than lactate threshold pace.
pacing_adjustments_by_track_distance.medium_intervals_1mile_2k: Executed approximately 3% to 6% slower than lactate threshold pace.
pacing_adjustments_by_track_distance.long_intervals_3k: Executed approximately 6% to 9% slower than lactate threshold pace.

easy_running_intensity_rule.heart_rate_cap: Strictly under 70% of maximum heart rate (Max HR).
easy_running_intensity_rule.effort_guidelines: RPE 2-3/10 for trained athletes; strictly RPE 3/10 for beginners.
easy_running_intensity_rule.purpose: Build aerobic capillary bed without autonomic or structural stress. Avoids 'zombie training' (easy runs being executed too fast).

muscle_tone_management.concept: Mechanical tension and muscular stiffness ('muscle tone') act as a primary recovery limiter alongside metabolic stress.
muscle_tone_management.application: Splitting threshold volume into morning and afternoon blocks (or shorter interval sets) maintains optimal neuromuscular elasticity without causing structural breakdown.

norwegian_custom_fartlek.definition: A structured 5-minute cycle fartlek used as a versatile alternative to rigid track reps.
norwegian_custom_fartlek.structure: 1 cycle = 2 min @ RPE 6-7/10 (7/10 effort) + 1 min @ RPE 5/10 (5/10 medium float) + 1 min @ RPE 7/10 (7/10 hard effort) + 1 min @ RPE 5/10 (5/10 medium float).
norwegian_custom_fartlek.execution: Repeat 4 to 8 cycles (20 to 40 minutes of total quality sub-threshold work). Great for standalone single threshold days or evening workouts.

kenyan_fartlek.definition: Continuous aerobic progression fartlek consisting of 1 min sub-threshold surge / 1 min floating recovery.
kenyan_fartlek.application: Introduced in early base phases and inside long runs to build rhythm, lactate shuttling, and mental focus without accumulating high lactate.

controlled_hill_workouts.definition: Short uphill reps on moderate gradients (4-6%) designed to maintain stride power, foot strike mechanics, and muscle tone without spiking blood lactate.
prescriptions: Beginners: 6-10 reps of 40s to 1 min hill jog @ RPE 4-5/10 with walk down rest.
Advanced: 15-20 reps of 200m uphill @ controlled 5K effort (jog down recovery).

integrated_long_run_workouts.concept: Embedding sub-threshold blocks or alternating pace segments into the second half of long easy runs to build durable race-specific aerobic power.

variations.alternating_kilometers: 1 km Easy (<70% Max HR) / 1 km @ T2 (Main threshold pace) / 1 km @ T1 (Lower threshold pace). Repeat for 6-12 km inside the long run.
variations.kenyan_fartlek_long_run: First 50-60% easy (<70% Max HR), followed by 20-30 minutes of (1 min sub-threshold / 1 min easy float).
variations.second_half_progression: First 60% easy (<70% Max HR); final 40% executed at steady sub-threshold effort (~1.8-2.2 mmol/L).

phase_1_base_foundation_building.primary_focus: High aerobic volume, low lactate accumulation, building structural muscle tone, and introducing track rep discipline.
phase_1_base_foundation_building.track_rep_distinction: Morning reps: 3k reps, 2k reps, 1 mile reps @ lower threshold (1.8-2.2 mmol/L). Evening reps: 1000m, 800m reps @ main threshold (2.5-3.0 mmol/L).
phase_1_base_foundation_building.long_run_and_fartlek: Easy long runs incorporating early Kenyan Fartlek blocks (1 min on / 1 min float).
phase_1_base_foundation_building.hill_integration: Weekly controlled hill sessions (15-20x 200m) to maintain power and muscle elasticity.

phase_2_specific_aerobic_development.primary_focus: Expanding sub-threshold density, refining pacing, and introducing alternating-week VO2max work.
phase_2_specific_aerobic_development.track_rep_distinction: Morning reps: 2k, 1 mile reps @ lower threshold. Evening reps: 800m, 600m, 400m reps or Norwegian Custom Fartlek cycles.
phase_2_specific_aerobic_development.long_run_and_fartlek: Integrated long runs with Alternating Kilometers (1 km Easy / 1 km T2 / 1 km T1).
phase_2_specific_aerobic_development.vo2max_alternate_weeks: Every 2nd week, replace Saturday hills/threshold with goal-race specific VO2 max workouts (e.g., 6-8x 800m fast or 3-4x 2k fast).

phase_3_race_specific_sharpening_and_con.primary_focus: Maximizing speed at threshold, race-pace confidence workouts, high turnover, and fine-tuning lactate clearing.
phase_3_race_specific_sharpening_and_con.track_rep_distinction: Morning reps: 1 mile, 1000m reps. Evening reps: High-turnover 400m and 200m track reps @ sub-threshold speed with strict 30-45s recovery.
phase_3_race_specific_sharpening_and_con.race_confidence_workouts: Goal-race specific simulation sessions (e.g., 5K runner doing 5x 1000m @ target race pace with controlled lactate; Marathoner doing 3x 5k @ marathon pace inside a 22 km run).
phase_3_race_specific_sharpening_and_con.vo2max_and_hills: Race-specific VO2 max workouts maintained every 14 days.

phase_4_taper_and_race_execution.primary_focus: Volume reduction by 30-50% while retaining high-frequency threshold touchpoints to preserve neuromuscular muscle tone and fresh legs.
phase_4_taper_and_race_execution.workout_adjustments: Short sub-threshold track sessions (e.g., 8-10x 400m or 5x 800m @ threshold pace with long recovery) 4 days before race day.

athlete_levels_and_starting_points.level_title: Total Beginner / Overweight / Non-Runner (<10 km/week or zero baseline)

starting_point.prerequisites: Physician clearance for exercise; ability to walk continuously for 20 minutes.
starting_point.training_experience: Zero formal running background; prone to over-exertion.

effort_and_pacing_rules.effort_mindset: MUST run strictly at RPE 3/10 (Very Light Jog). Beginners mistakenly think running requires RPE 8/10; force them to stay at RPE 3/10.
effort_and_pacing_rules.hills_effort: RPE 4-5/10 (Slightly higher effort, but strictly controlled).

weekly_schedule.monday: Rest Day or Light 20 min Walking.
weekly_schedule.tuesday: Walk-Run Session 1 — 10 reps of (40s light jog @ RPE 3/10 + 2 min walk rest). Total run time = 6.6 min.
weekly_schedule.thursday: Walk-Run Session 2 (Hill Control) — 8 reps of (40s light uphill jog @ RPE 4-5/10 + 2 min walk down rest).
weekly_schedule.saturday: Walk-Run Session 3 — 10 reps of (50s light jog @ RPE 3/10 + 2 min walk rest).
weekly_schedule.sunday: Long Easy Walk-Run — 25-30 minutes total (1 min light jog @ RPE 3/10 / 2 min walk).

seasonal_progression_rules.phase_1_base: Week 1: 40s run / 2 min walk. Week 2: 50s run / 2 min walk. Week 3: 60s run / 2 min walk.
seasonal_progression_rules.phase_2_development: Transition to 90s run / 90s walk, maintaining RPE 3/10 strictly.
seasonal_progression_rules.phase_3_sharpening: Achieve 3-5 min continuous running blocks @ RPE 3/10 with 1 min walk rest.

athlete_levels_and_starting_points.level_title: Early Beginner / Low Fitness (15 - 20 km/week, can run 5K continuous but unfit)

starting_point.prerequisites: Able to complete a 5K walk-run or slow continuous run without stopping.
starting_point.training_experience: Basic aerobic base, easily fatigued by fast running.

weekly_schedule.tuesday: Run-Walk Threshold Session — 6-8 reps of (3 min light run @ RPE 4/10 + 1-2 min walk rest).
weekly_schedule.wednesday: Easy Walk-Run — 30 min (4 min run / 1 min walk @ RPE 3/10).
weekly_schedule.thursday: Controlled Hill Session — 8-10 reps of (1 min uphill jog @ RPE 5/10 + 90s walk down rest).
weekly_schedule.saturday: Short Fartlek Session — 20 min total: (2 min RPE 5/10 + 1 min easy walk/jog + 1 min RPE 6/10 + 1 min easy walk/jog) x 4 cycles.
weekly_schedule.sunday: Short Long Run — 40 min total duration (continuous easy run @ RPE 3-4/10 or 5 min run / 1 min walk).

seasonal_progression_rules.phase_1_base: Build from 3 min run / 2 min walk up to 5 min run / 1 min walk.
seasonal_progression_rules.phase_2_development: Introduce continuous 10-15 min sub-threshold blocks @ RPE 5/10.
seasonal_progression_rules.phase_3_sharpening: Complete continuous 5K run @ RPE 5-6/10 with strong pacing discipline.

starting_point.weekly_mileage_range: 30 - 50 km / week (approx. 20 - 30 miles/week) or 3 - 5 training hours/week.
starting_point.prerequisites: Minimum 3-6 months of regular easy running without injury.
starting_point.training_experience: New to systematic track threshold work.

weekly_schedule.tuesday: Track Threshold Session 1 — AM or PM: 4-5x 1 Mile reps @ Golden Zone lower threshold pace (3-6% slower than threshold) with 60s jog rest.
weekly_schedule.wednesday: Easy Run (35-45 min strictly <70% Max HR).
weekly_schedule.friday: Easy Run (35-45 min strictly <70% Max HR).
weekly_schedule.saturday: Track Threshold Session 2 OR Fartlek — AM: 8-10x 800m reps @ sub-threshold pace with 45s rest OR 20 min Norwegian Custom Fartlek.
weekly_schedule.sunday: Long Easy Run (60-75 min strictly <70% Max HR).

seasonal_progression_rules.phase_1_base: Focus on 1 Mile reps in AM and 800m reps in PM; incorporate Kenyan Fartlek (1 min on / 1 min float) into early long runs.
seasonal_progression_rules.phase_2_development: Expand total threshold volume from 20 min to 30 min per session; introduce Norwegian Custom Fartlek.
seasonal_progression_rules.phase_3_sharpening: Transition PM track reps to 400m reps @ fast threshold speed with 30s recovery.

starting_point.weekly_mileage_range: 40 - 60 km / week (approx. 25 - 40 miles/week) or 5 - 7 training hours/week.
starting_point.prerequisites: Consistent running history for 1+ years; able to run 5 days per week.
starting_point.training_experience: Familiar with track reps, heart rate zones, and tempo work.

athlete_levels_and_starting_points.prescribed_model: Full Norwegian Singles (3x Sub-Threshold Workouts/Week) OR Intro Double Threshold (1 double day + 1 single).

weekly_schedule.monday: Easy Recovery Run (45 min <70% Max HR).
weekly_schedule.tuesday: Long Sub-Threshold Track Session — AM: 3x 2k reps or 4x 1 Mile reps @ lower threshold pace (~2.0 mmol/L, 78-82% HR) with 60s rest.
weekly_schedule.wednesday: Easy Recovery Run (50-60 min <70% Max HR).
weekly_schedule.thursday: Short Sub-Threshold Track Session — PM: 10-12x 800m or 12-15x 400m reps @ main threshold pace (~2.8 mmol/L, 82-86% HR) with 45s rest OR Norwegian Custom Fartlek (30 min).
weekly_schedule.friday: Easy Recovery Run (40 min <70% Max HR) or Rest Day.
weekly_schedule.saturday: Controlled Hills OR Alternate Week VO2max Session — 15x 200m hill reps OR 6x 800m fast reps @ 5K pace.
weekly_schedule.sunday: Integrated Long Run (80-100 min) — First half easy (<70% Max HR); second half includes 6 km of Alternating Kilometers (1 km Easy / 1 km T2 / 1 km T1).

seasonal_progression_rules.phase_1_base: Morning reps: 3k and 2k reps. Evening reps: 1000m and 800m reps. Weekly hills.
seasonal_progression_rules.phase_2_development: Morning reps: 2k and 1 Mile reps. Evening reps: 800m and 400m reps. Alternate-week VO2 max sessions (e.g., 6x 800m fast).
seasonal_progression_rules.phase_3_sharpening: PM reps shift to 400m/200m track reps @ high-turnover threshold pace; execute Goal-Race Confidence workout 14 days before race.

starting_point.weekly_mileage_range: 80 - 160+ km / week (approx. 50 - 100+ miles/week) or 9 - 15+ training hours/week.
starting_point.prerequisites: Multi-year high-volume background; high structural durability.
starting_point.training_experience: Routine blood lactate testing, precise pulse monitoring, track mastery.

athlete_levels_and_starting_points.prescribed_model: Classic Norwegian Double Threshold Model (2x Double Threshold Days + Saturday Quality/VO2max).

weekly_schedule.monday: Easy Recovery Run AM (50 min) + Easy Recovery Run PM (40 min) strictly <70% Max HR.
weekly_schedule.tuesday: Double Threshold Day 1 — AM: Track 2x 3k + 2x 2k reps @ lower threshold (1.8-2.2 mmol/L, 75-82% HR) with 60s rest; PM: Track 10-12x 1000m or 12-15x 800m reps @ main threshold (2.5-3.2 mmol/L, 82-88% HR) with 45s rest.
weekly_schedule.wednesday: Easy Recovery Run AM (60 min) + Easy Recovery Run PM (40 min) strictly <70% Max HR.
weekly_schedule.thursday: Double Threshold Day 2 — AM: Track 4-5x 1 Mile reps @ lower threshold (1.8-2.3 mmol/L); PM: Track 20-25x 400m reps or Norwegian Custom Fartlek (35 min) @ main threshold (2.8-3.4 mmol/L).
weekly_schedule.friday: Easy Recovery Run (50-60 min <70% Max HR).
weekly_schedule.saturday: Specific Quality / Alternate VO2max Day — AM: 20x 200m hill reps OR 4x 2k fast reps @ race target pace; PM: Light easy recovery jog (30 min).
weekly_schedule.sunday: Integrated Long Aerobic Run (100-130 min) — Incorporating Kenyan Fartlek or Alternating Kilometers in the second half.

seasonal_progression_rules.phase_1_base: Focus on high double-threshold volume using 3k, 2k, 1 mile reps in AM and 1000m, 800m reps in PM.
seasonal_progression_rules.phase_2_development: Maintain AM volume with 2k/1 Mile reps; transition PM reps to 800m/400m; insert race-specific VO2max workouts on alternate Saturdays.
seasonal_progression_rules.phase_3_sharpening: PM sessions feature high-turnover 400m / 200m track reps @ sub-threshold speed with 30s rest; execute final Race-Confidence session 10-12 days out.

5k_10k_race_goal.focus: High density of threshold track reps, short float rests, and Saturday high-turnover VO2 max reps.
key_workouts: PM Threshold Track Reps: 12-15x 800m or 20-25x 400m reps @ main threshold speed.
Alternate Saturday VO2max: 6-8x 800m fast reps @ 3K/5K pace with 2 min recovery.
Race Confidence Session: 5x 1000m @ 5K target pace with 90s rest, keeping lactate controlled below 4.0 mmol/L.
20x 200m hill reps for stride power and muscle tone maintenance.

half_marathon_race_goal.focus: Extending interval rep length (2k, 1 mile, 3k) in the lower Golden Zone threshold range.
key_workouts: AM Threshold Track Reps: 2x 3k + 2x 2k reps @ Golden Zone lower threshold.
Alternate Saturday VO2max: 4x 2k fast reps @ 10K/Half Marathon pace.
Integrated Long Run: 100-115 min with 8-10 km of Alternating Kilometers (1 km Easy / 1 km T2 / 1 km T1).

marathon_race_goal.focus: Maximizing aerobic efficiency, fat oxidation, and sub-threshold volume inside long runs.
key_workouts: AM Threshold Track Reps: 3-4x 2k or 3x 3k reps @ marathon sub-threshold effort (1.8-2.2 mmol/L).
Race Confidence Session: 22-25 km Long Run with 3x 5k @ target Marathon pace inside.
Integrated Long Run: 2.0 to 2.5 hours with last 40% executed at continuous sub-threshold effort.
Flat weekly volume repeated over 12-16 week blocks.

rules_for_workout_generation: Enforce strict RPE limits for beginners (Level 0 and 0.5 must stay at RPE 3/10 during runs).
Always make morning double threshold sessions longer in distance (3k, 2k, 1 mile) and lower in lactate (1.8-2.3 mmol/L) than evening sessions.
Always make evening double threshold sessions shorter in distance (1k, 800m, 400m, 200m) and slightly higher in lactate/speed (2.5-3.5 mmol/L).
Ensure all easy runs stay strictly under 70% Max HR.
Incorporate long-run workout variations (Alternating km, Kenyan Fartlek) in the second half of long runs for Intermediate and Advanced athletes.
Swap hill reps for race-specific VO2 max track workouts every other week as race day approaches.
common_traps_to_avoid: Zombie Training: running easy days too fast and hard days not precisely controlled, resulting in constant chronic fatigue.
Overshooting Lactate: turning controlled sub-threshold workouts into high-lactate VO2max sessions.
Prescribing Double Threshold days to athletes running under 50 km/week who lack aerobic durability.

strength_and_prehab._note: Not part of the new Norwegian Method source document (which is running/threshold-only) — carried over from the prior brain because the app still assigns type:'strength' sessions and needs real exercise content for them.
strength_and_prehab.purpose: Injury prevention over performance enhancement. Target the 'weakest link'.
strength_and_prehab.exercises: Hang Clean (explosiveness), Squats/Bulgarian Split Squats (stability), Step-ups, Hip Thrusts, Calf Raises.
